Circuitborn. Normalized Bad Eden ancestry root.

Select one heritage separately when building the character: Exo-Knight, Parallax, Salvage, Synapse.

This root grants the shared Circuitborn core trait package (Firmware of Identity) and preserves live UUID compatibility for the four Line items.

“You are not a robot. You are a decision the world keeps making about itself. The networks are alive and they recognize you on sight.”

Firmware of Identity. You do not eat, drink, or sleep. You enter maintenance trance when you rest. You reroll the lowest die on checks against poison and disease, and you are immune to magical sleep.

Attention Resonance. 1/Soma Break, when a creature you can see is intensely focused on you, you may regain either one spent Bad Eden OP (a category you used this scene) or Integrity equal to your tier.

Informational Matrix Sense. You can feel active networks: radio, signal, ritual, rumor.

Line Memory. Choose one Circuitborn line (Exo-Knight, Parallax, Salvage, Synapse). Your line grants Tier powers as you level.

description.value:
“You are not a robot. You are a decision the world keeps making about itself.”

Firmware of Identity. You do not eat, drink, or sleep. You enter maintenance trance when you rest. You reroll the lowest die on checks against poison and disease, and you are immune to magical sleep.

Attention Resonance. 1/Soma Break, when a creature you can see is intensely focused on you (ally or enemy; GM adjudicates), you may regain either (a) one spent Bad Eden OP (a category you used this scene) or (b) Integrity equal to your tier.

Informational Matrix Sense. You can feel active networks: radio, signal, ritual, rumor. You reroll the lowest die on checks to identify surveillance, hidden speakers, encoded messages, or noospheric “attention traps.”

Glitch-Surge. When you drop to 0 Integrity, you can choose to emit a controlled burst of static (no damage, but loud and disorienting) before you fall. In Bad Eden play, this is a perfect excuse for weird consequences.

description.value:
Circuitborn Line. The war-plate. Made for impact, for holding the line, for being the thing the squad puts between itself and whatever just came through the gate.

“Captain Robot is not a robot. You are. Try not to make it weird about him.”

Exo-Knight. You are a sentient chassis built around the principle of presence. When you stand somewhere, that ground belongs to your faction until something stronger walks you off it.

Traits

  • Creature Type. Humanoid (Construct-Living).

  • Chassis Lean. Your chassis is built around VIO (Violence)—expressed primarily through Tier powers.

  • Bulwark Frame. When an ally within 1 square of you is hit by an attack, you may use your reaction to impose 3d10 keep lowest 2 on the attack roll (1/Soma Break).

advancement.title: Exo-Knight Tier I
advancement.hint: Gain your Exo-Knight Line Tier I power (Shield Projector).

description.value:
“If you stand near me, you’re harder to kill. That’s the point.”

Shield Projector (tier/Soma Break). When a creature you can see within 6 squares is hit, you can use your reaction to project a barrier. Reduce the damage by 1d6 + your tier.

⚙ ENGINE NOTE — Frame & Ruin are now ◆ Surge. Read Frame Die as banked Surge spent defensively, Ruin Charge as Surge spent offensively. Bulwarks bank +1 Surge when they take Integrity damage (max +2/round; +3 w/ Polarity Mastery on Mountain). Path kits live in the ◆ Surge menu. Automated: Polarity Mastery (melee strike, base die ≥ 8 → +1 Surge 1/round), Anchor or Advance + The Breach (clickable, 1/scene).

"Set your feet. The line forms on you."

The Bulwark is the wall — and the wall runs on Surge, like everyone, but yours arrives the hard way: every time you take Integrity damage you bank +1 Surge (max +2/round). You eat the blow and turn it into the power to anchor, erupt, or hold. At zero Surge you still stand in the way; soak one hit and your turn opens up.

The Fortress (spent via Surge — Bulwark only)

  • Brace Wall (1) — you and adjacent allies gain DR equal to Tier this round.
  • Bulwark Stance (6) — adjacent allies share your defenses until your next turn.
  • Anchor (5) — you and one ally become immune to forced movement and crowd-control until next round.
  • Mass Aegis (8) — allies within Tier squares gain +Tier to every defense this round.
  • Sanctum (9) — immune to one damage type for a round.
  • Mythic Stand (10) — invulnerable until the start of your next turn.

These were always the Bulwark's birthright; they no longer leak into everyone else's menu. Frame Dice and Ruin Charges endure as the strategic layer — Catastrophic Entry still sunders armor and breaches structures, Ruin still cuts a Siege's cost — and both refill on a Soma Break.

The world has two ways of saying no to change. You learn one of them today.

On gaining Bulwark Initiation 1 you receive:

  • Skill rank +1 in Athletics (Violence).

  • Skill rank +1 in one tool of your choice (any single tool tracked as a skill on your sheet).

  • Violence OP cap +3 and Siege OP cap +2 on the faction your character belongs to.

  • Your Frame Dice pool comes online (persistence — d8 dice, spend to absorb hits or fuel doctrine effects). Pool max = max(2, ceil((Violence value + Bulwark Initiation) / 3)), capped at 8.

  • Your Ruin Charges pool comes online (inevitability — single-use charges, spend to fuel offensive doctrine effects). Same pool-size formula.

Both pools refill on a Soma Break. How you generate them depends on your chosen Path; see your doctrine's L1 feature.

system.source: Bad Eden Originals — Sprint F (2026 rules)

description.value:
"You do not stop. They learn this the hard way."

Doctrine: Momentum is the point — geography deciding to move.

The Avalanche is mass that arrives all at once. Your Surge spends are forward motion made lethal: barrel through, crash home, and — when it matters — become a thing nothing in the world can currently stop.

Path (spent via Surge)

  • Roll Forward (1) — your next Strike +Tier d6, and the target is knocked Prone.
  • Crash (3) — your next Strike lands as a max-die crit; the target is Staggered.
  • Unstoppable (5) — immune to forced-movement/CC this round; your next Strike ignores resistances and knocks the target Prone.

“You move before the map exists.”

Archetype (Bad Eden): The Fool (Catalyst). You are motion before certainty, risk before consensus, and the destabilizing force that turns unknown ground into lived reality.

Archetype Effects

  • Faction Edge. Your archetype strengthens exploration, scouting, improvisation, and risky openings. This Archetype is associated with +1 Intrigue and +1 Logistics in faction calculus.
  • Tier Engine. See this Archetype’s Tier feats (Tier 1–4) for your full tactical and strategic toolkit.

attributes (Archetype ASI)

Common patterns include:

  • Wild Pathfinder: +2 Intrigue, +1 Soul
  • Restless Scout: +2 Soul, +1 Intrigue
  • Improvisational Menace: +1 Intrigue, +1 Soul, +1 Presence

description.value:
Crew Type (Bad Eden): Ironbound Ascendants.

“Height is not terrain. It is policy.”

Ironbound Ascendants make strongholds out of bad footing and turn cliffs into arguments. They understand supply lines, choke valleys, and the spiritual value of making your enemies climb tired. If a mountain matters, they intend to own the meaning of it.

  • Tactical Identity: You gain a skill rank in Athletics and Athletics.
  • Strategic Identity: Your faction starts with +1 Logistics OPs.

Victory - Endurance becomes momentum. +1 Violence, +1 Culture OPs

Netzach is passion that refuses extinction. It rewards morale, persistence, and the emotional drive to keep moving when a lesser faction would break or quietly go home.

Occult Association (Bad Eden): Biomancer / Fleshcrafter.

“You don’t survive the world. You rewrite what Athletics means.”

Biomancers do not treat life as sacred. They treat it as modifiable.

Where Alchemists convert matter and Shamans negotiate with ecosystems, Biomancers operate at a more intimate scale: flesh, bone, instinct, and adaptation. To them, evolution is not a process. It is a toolkit.

The Great Work, in their hands, is not about restoring what was lost. It is about building something that can survive what is coming.

How Biomancers pursue the Great Work:

  • By modifying bodies to survive hostile conditions
  • By reducing loss through biological adaptation
  • By converting harm into resilience
  • By treating mutation as both tool and risk

Resonance: Yesod / Life-State — transformation, embodiment, and the unstable boundary between identity and function.

Tell-tales: asymmetry, controlled mutation, eyes that adapt faster than they should.

Faction Effect (Passive):

  • +1 specialty edge on Athletics, endurance, or recovery-related OP rolls

Cost Principle: adaptation changes you. Expect mutation, instability, and moments where you are no longer certain what “baseline” meant.

Tier 1 (Level 1) — The Fool (Catalyst)

  • Tactical: You gain a skill rank in Athletics and Athletics.
  • Strategic: Your faction's passive OP bias now follows the base Archetype file.

Nothing that moves can be stopped — and movement, for you, is what makes you real.

Mode: Unstoppable Force / drift: Toward.

You generate Frame Dice when you end a movement, not when you start one. When you move at least half your speed in a turn and end that turn with a successful Violence-attribute action or weapon strike, gain 1 Frame Die. Maximum 1 Frame Die generated per turn from this feature.

Your Frame pool refreshes on a Soma Break. Pool max comes from your Bulwark class feature: max(2, ceil((Violence value + Bulwark Initiation) / 3)), capped at 8.

description.value:
Breach Specialist

Everything has a seam. Most people just don’t look.

Rules

You gain skill rank with thieves’ tools. If you already have it, you gain mastery.

When you hit an object, door, barrier, or construct with a weapon attack, you may treat the attack as dealing maximum damage to the target’s objects-only resistances (GM adjudication). Once you do, you can’t do so again until the start of your next turn.

Arriving is the strike.

When you move 2 squares or more in a straight line in a turn and finish with a melee weapon strike, you may spend 1 Ruin Charge as part of that strike. If you do:

  • The strike's damage is also applied to every creature and breakable object in a 1 square line directly behind your target, in your direction of travel. Each secondary target may make a Body defense check (DC 12 + your Initiation tier × 2) — on success, the secondary target takes half damage; on a failed check the full strike damage applies.
  • The original target is pushed 2 squares in the direction of your charge (no save).

description.value:
Signature move. Once a scene, you choose which kind of inevitability you are.

Anchor or Advance — 1/scene (recovers on Soma Break). As part of any action on your turn, declare a stance. The chosen stance lasts until the end of your next turn:

  • Anchor. You cannot be moved against your will by any effect short of a Heroic-DC (22) push from a creature of your size or larger. Forced movement, knockback, teleportation targeting you, banishment, and dimensional swap effects all fail.

  • Advance. You cannot be prevented from reaching a destination you declare on the same action. Difficult terrain, conditions that halve speed, opportunity reactions, and zone-of-control effects do not stop your movement toward that point. You may still take damage along the way.

Doctrine features at L5+ extend or modify which stance you favor.

system.source: Bad Eden Core Feats v1 (2024 rules)

description.value:
Adaptive Defense

Defense is not denial. It is management.

Rules

When you are hit by an attack you can see, you may use your reaction to reduce the damage by an amount equal to your skill rank bonus + your Violence or Intrigue value (your choice).

Difficult terrain is for people who pause.

Your movement speed cannot be reduced below half your base speed by any effect, condition, surface, or creature short of a physical barrier substantial enough to stop a charging rhino (GM call). This includes — but is not limited to — difficult terrain, grease, web, the restrained condition, the prone condition's stand-up cost, slowed/snared effects, and being grappled by a creature your size or smaller.

You still take damage from traps and hazardous terrain along your path; you simply do not stop for them. You may end movement voluntarily.

system.requirements: Path of the Avalanche, Bulwark Initiation 9

system.source: Bad Eden Bulwark + Shadow Courier v1.0 (RFI-native rules)

description.value:
Your Path's resource-generation rules learn a second voice.

At Bulwark Initiation 11, your doctrine's pool-generation logic extends. Apply the rule for your chosen Path:

  • Path of the Avalanche. In addition to your normal Frame generation, gain 1 Frame Die when you score a successful melee strike (any roll where at least one die rolled before explosions shows ≥ 8). 1/turn cap.

  • Path of the Mountain. In addition to your normal Ruin generation, gain 1 Ruin Charge when you take damage from a single instance of any source while remaining upright. 1/turn cap.

  • Path of the Cataclyst. Once per round, you may swap 1 Frame Die for 1 Ruin Charge or vice versa as a free action (no action economy cost). The transferred die/charge is not 'charged' (see Cataclyst L1).

Battlefield Presence

People fight better when you are near.

Rules

Allies within 2 squares of you reroll the lowest die on the first defense checks they make against being Shaken or charmed each combat.

system.source: Bad Eden Bulwark + Shadow Courier v1.0 (RFI-native rules)

description.value:
Declare the line. The line happens.

The Breach — 1/scene (recovers on Soma Break). On your turn, declare a straight-line path to a destination within your maximum movement for the turn. You move to that destination, and any physical barrier in your way breaks open as you pass:

  • Wooden walls, doors, panes, and fortifications up to Hard hardness (DC 18) are broken open.

  • Stone walls and reinforced doors require a Violence attribute check vs Heroic DC 22 to pass through; on failure you stop adjacent to the barrier and lose the rest of the movement.

  • Any creature of size huge or smaller occupying a space along the line takes (Violence value + Bulwark Initiation) kinetic damage, damageFlavor: bludgeoning, and is knocked prone. They do not block your path.

You arrive upright, in your normal initiative slot, with whatever debris a person carries when they have just opened a wall.

description.value:
Backline Commander

You don’t need to be closest to steer the fight.

Rules

As a Bonus action, choose one ally who can see or hear you within 6 squares That ally may immediately move up to 2 squares without provoking reaction strikes.

You can use this principle a number of times equal to your skill rank bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Sanctuary.

system.source: Bad Eden Bulwark + Shadow Courier v1.0 (RFI-native rules)

description.value:
You no longer push against the world's resistances. They simply do not apply to you.

At Bulwark Initiation 16, both poles of your inevitability harden:

  • Ruin bypass. Damage you deal as part of any feature that explicitly spends a Ruin Charge ignores all kinetic-type resistance and any cover/structure damage-reduction the target would otherwise apply. (Energy/Sephirotic/etc. resistances still apply.)

  • Frame absorption. When a Frame Die you spend reduces incoming damage (per a doctrine feature or Tier 2 Anchor stance), reduce the incoming damage by an additional Violence value points before the Frame Die roll is added.

system.source: Bad Eden Bulwark + Shadow Courier v1.0 (RFI-native rules)

description.value:
Movement is now a doctrine of the body.

While you have at least 1 Frame Die in your pool:

  • You are immune to forced movement, the staggered condition, and any effect that would stun, paralyze, or render you unconscious without first reducing your integrity to 0.

  • At the start of your turn you may spend any number of Frame Dice. For each one spent, roll the die and add the result to your movement speed (in feet) for that turn only.

  • You may pass through the space occupied by any creature or unattended object softer than reinforced stone (GM call) without stopping. You do not provoke reactions while doing so.

Fluid Footwork

You move like the fight is trying to catch up with you.

Rules

Your movement increases by 2 squares Additionally, when you make a melee attack against a creature, that creature can’t make reaction strikes against you for the rest of the turn (hit or miss).

Bladed Tempo

Your weapons are punctuation.

Rules

When you hit with a melee weapon attack, you may immediately draw or stow a weapon, or shift 1 square without provoking reaction strikes.
